title: Rewrite BotTools and the private repositories
issueTitle: Phase 0 · 7.2 — Rewrite BotTools and the private repositories
function: BotTools and the private repositories still carry purged paths in their histories, 39, 199 and 7,259 purged blobs, and every root commit holds one, so every commit and every branch of the three changes in the rewrite. This unit rewrites them in that order, each from its mirror checked unchanged since the preparation unit, and each starting only once the one before it has passed its exit tests: the rewrite with its post-run checks and the scan before the push; one atomic push per repository, on request, with an explicit lease on every branch's recorded tip after a dry run of the same line, two branches for BotTools and the first private repository and one for the second; the outcome classed from counted markers and read back at every branch, with a push never repeated blindly; per-ref verification, with BotTools' webhook deliveries counted right after its push; and a fresh mirror with its exit tests, with BotTools' pull-request residual counted. Unit 2 of #27, with no version moved; it changes no checkout, and its landing carries documents only.

downstream.summary: Since the first private repository's push it shares no commit with the server's branches. This unit did not touch it; the clone replacement (#42) replaces it. No fork of the three repositories exists.

The three mirrors were rewritten in place and their untouched backups stay as they were; a fresh mirror of each, the unit's data file, the grant's wording, its scratch folder and the scans' reports were added. The tool folders were not changed; the phase's cleanup deletes the workspace.

The unit's own record folder, and new files beside the preparation unit's records in each repository's folder, which were not written, each folder with its checksum list; the run log gained the unit's lines.

Its local state changed at the owner's console only: the grant section of this unit's job, the deny rule on the lease push lifted for the job, and three allow lines, one per push, in the global settings file it reads, with no restart. All three stay until the section moves to history, when the deny rule is restored and the allow lines are removed.

The unit's plan, consequences and as-built record, one link line in the parent consequences, dated notes on the parent design's §2.4 and §12, where the build changed what they describe, and the regenerated boards; no README change and no CHANGELOG entry.

adaptation.who: The owner, before the unit runs
adaptation.summary: Gave the grant section and the lift of the deny rule on the lease push. The lift did not yet hold in every settings file the request service loads at BotTools' first call, which the service's own check refused before anything ran; three allow lines, one per push, then went into the global settings file the running service reads, and no restart was needed.

Its data file names this unit in `from`: each repository's stage-8 marker, its records with their checksum list, the time of each push, recorded as the time the push was classed, BotTools' delivery counts and every branch at its rewritten tip. It follows promptly, as the events of BotTools' push cover 30 days from 2026-11-15 and can lag by up to 6 hours.

Its data file names this unit in `from`: the first private repository's stage-8 marker, with its maps, its manifest and its untouched backup. For its own requests, it takes what the parent design's §2.4 now says of allow lines and restarts, in its dated note.
It takes every record of this unit with its checksum list. No default-rule finding arose, so none is handed on.

changes.what: Three allow lines, one per push, went into the request service's global settings file at once, and the service ran BotTools' refused request again with no restart.
changes.why: Once the line was in the file the running service reads, it applied it, so a restart had nothing left to do; the later pushes met their lines already in place and neither was refused (the as-built record, deviations 1 and 2).

changes.what: The lift of the deny rule held in one of the two settings files the request service loads when the unit started, and in both from 19:09Z; BotTools' first call was refused by the service's own check before anything ran.
changes.why: The plan's path for such a call ran as designed: the state read named every branch at its old tip, nothing was sent twice, and the service ran the request again itself (consequences, A4).

changes.what: The time recorded for each push is the time the push was classed, 111, 68 and 77 seconds after GitHub's own push time.
changes.why: The tool writes it when it classes the push as pushed, the first moment the unit knows the push landed; the residual measurement compares it with the events' window in whole days, so the difference changes nothing there (deviation 3).

changes.what: The clone replacement also takes, for its own requests, the parent design's dated note on allow lines and restarts.
changes.why: The build showed an allow line takes effect without a restart, so the parent design's §2.4 and §12 carry dated notes on it.

changes.what: No default-rule finding is handed on to the residual report and cleanup.
changes.why: None arose in BotTools or either private repository, before a push or on a fresh mirror.

changes.what: The parent design took dated notes on its §2.4 and §12.
changes.why: The build changed what they describe: an allow line placed in the file the running request service reads took effect without a restart.
